name: Dark mode and theme
plain: Reads whether the system uses dark or light appearance.
meaning: Weak habit signal; one bit, but often scheduled so it also hints at sunset time.

limits.headline: Can see whether your phone is in dark or light mode
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app opens or you switch themes
can: Check if the system uses dark or light appearance
Switch its own colors to match
cannot: See your wallpaper, brightness or schedule
Tell who you are on its own, but it is one bit in a fingerprint

story.what_it_is: An app sees whether your phone is in dark or light appearance.

marketing.name: Dark Mode
marketing.pitch: Apple's system wide dark look that apps can follow so screens are easier on the eyes at night.

marketing.name: Dark theme
marketing.pitch: Android lets apps follow a system dark theme, which can save battery on OLED screens.

story.for_you: You flip a switch or let the phone change at sunset, and apps follow. Your eyes thank you at night. You never see the apps read the setting.
story.for_makers: Makers want apps to feel native and to save battery. The setting is a single bit, but it often follows a schedule, so it can hint at sunset time and where you are.

use_cases.example: A video app turns its menus dark when you watch at night so the screen is easier to look at.
A game picks a darker menu theme when your phone is in dark mode.
A chat app switches its bubbles to dark colors to match your phone.
A reading app follows dark mode so late night reading is calmer.
A tracker adds dark mode to a profile, which helps match the same phone across sites.
An advertiser changes ad colors at night so ads blend in with the app.

story.android_note: Android apps read it through the night mode setting, and many follow it automatically.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps read it from the user interface style, and may change when the schedule flips.
